title: tar member loads are 512-byte record aligned
summary: The normal ustar header occupies 512 bytes, and padding after the file data pushes the next header to the entire 512-byte record boundary.
detail: When the ordinary file size is 513, the data area occupies two records; the content is only 513 bytes.
boundary: Padding bytes are not included in the file size, and the pax extension header itself also consumes archive records.
relevance: When locating the second file from a continuous archive stream, avoid treating the padding area as a file header.
